- Keep these instructions current
- Sanitize string HTML in table cells, overview cards, settings, option/merge-tag labels, and route fills with `sanitizeHtml` from `@hizzlewp/components` immediately before insertion, after interpolation and navigation-link preparation. Preserve consumer formatting and `data-navigate-collection`; raw fields and REST `.rendered` values are not trusted HTML. Keep React-node content on its React rendering path.
- Datastore create/update responses honor validated `context`, defaulting to `edit`. Hizzle saves request `view` by default and cache the response in the requested context. Successful saves invalidate other cached contexts of the record and collection queries so filtering, ordering, and pagination totals refresh.
- Reconcile local edits against raw server values in every response context. Clear matching edits while preserving differing edits and fields omitted by partial responses; successful saves also clear the edits submitted in that request.
- Add explanatory comments when changing behavior whose purpose may be unclear. Explain the reason, relevant invariant, or edge case rather than restating the code.
- Receive single-record responses as objects and collection responses as arrays. Single reads and saves update item caches without replacing list membership or pagination metadata.
- Record hooks accept REST parameters through options.query and use that query for record reads, edited baselines, and the default save context. _fields selects fields in view or edit context. Export downloads use direct REST requests and component-local state, never the record cache. Reuse saved cached records only when query resolution, membership, field availability, and export eligibility are known. Export pickers and initial selections exclude fields that explicitly omit export context; missing context metadata remains selectable for older datastore releases.

- Share page-size options from the store constants through the records package. After real list responses, derive completed page-size resolutions from that response's offset, row count, and total. Include partial final pages and do not scan previous resolution metadata. Explicit invalidation must continue to fetch; sparse lists must not appear complete.

- Normalize collection pagination at the store-UI boundary through usePreparedQuery so reads and Refresh use identical arguments. Keep WordPress resolution actions and selector hooks unchanged. Expose normalizeCollectionQuery for consumers that opt in; finish one normalized entry per covered page and page size.
